title: Two North Koreans Seek Asylum in Japan
seoTitle: Two North Koreans seek asylum in Japan
subtitle: North Korean delegation arrives in Nagoya with possibility of defection
excerpt: Two members of the North Korean delegation participating in the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games are considering seeking asylum in Japan instead of returning home.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Gazeta do Povo, Portal Mie, O GLOBO
contentHtml:
Two members of the North Korean delegation participating in the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games are considering seeking asylum in Japan instead of returning to their country. The news, reported by the South Korean magazine Monthly Chosun and confirmed by sources from Japan's Cabinet Intelligence and Research Office, marks the first participation of a delegation of similar size in Japan since 1985.

Why the Case Is Trending Now

The information emerged on September 22, 2026, when Monthly Chosun magazine reported that two members of the North Korean delegation expressed a preference for seeking asylum in Japan. The development immediately garnered widespread attention in sports and international media, as it represents an unprecedented situation at an international sporting event in Japan.

Who Are the Asylum Seekers?

The names of the two individuals have not been disclosed, and it is not certain whether they are athletes, technical staff members, or North Korean officials. The delegation comprises approximately 180 people, including Sports Minister Kim Il-guk.

Source of the Information

The information was obtained through a source connected to Japan's Cabinet Intelligence and Research Office, an intelligence agency of the Japanese government, and the General Association of Korean Residents in Japan, known as Chongryon.

Asylum Request Status

As of now, there is no confirmation that formal asylum requests have been filed with Japanese authorities. The Japanese government has not yet commented on the matter, and it is not certain whether the requests have already been submitted.

Historical Context

This marks the first time a North Korean delegation has participated in an international sporting event in Japan since the Kobe Universiade (World University Games) held in 1985. Japan typically restricts the entry of North Korean citizens due to sanctions imposed on the country but made an exception for participation in this sporting event.

With information from Gazeta do Povo, Portal Mie, O GLOBO.
